definition: Scope is the region of a program where a name is visible. With lexical scope, the usual rule, a name is visible in the block where it is declared and in blocks nested inside that one. Code outside that region cannot use the name.
prompt: What is scope in a program?
details: An inner binding can shadow an outer one of the same name. Inside the inner block, the outer name is hidden.
examples: A loop variable that exists only inside the loop
A function parameter that is invisible to other functions
